requirements.title: Input and output statements define reading, writing, and optional editing
requirements.definition: Input statements transfer data from external media or internal files to internal storage and are called reading; output statements transfer data from internal storage to external media or internal files and are called writing; some input/output statements specify editing.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

S12.1-001 I/O records/files runtime fixtures: the internal formatted-transfer program initializes a character internal file to '#', writes exact characters with WRITE(record,'(I3,1X,A)'), then initializes integer and character input targets to distinctive sentinels and READs the same record back with the same explicit format. Exact record text, IOSTAT zero, and changed target values prove reading, writing, and specified editing without external representation assumptions.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.

S12.1-001 I/O records/files fixture boundaries: These fixtures are single-image positive runtime observations over internal CHARACTER files, scratch external files, and conservative local named files created in the execution working directory and deleted by the program. They assert only exact integers/logicals/characters, LEN before character equality, IOSTAT zero, and equality with the named IOSTAT_END constant. They do not assert byte sizes, record marker layout, IOMSG text, numeric IOSTAT values, ambient file existence, path syntax beyond the chosen local names, preconnected file identity, coarray image interactions, stream/record correspondence, or required diagnostics for mismatched forms/nonexistent files. Remaining facets stay pending with their source-accounting rationale.

S12.1-002 I/O records/files runtime fixtures: the external formatted-record program opens a scratch sequential formatted external file, INQUIREs OPENED=.true., writes records, REWINDs, and reads them in order. The REWIND is load-bearing because deleting it leaves the file position at terminal point; the INQUIRE logical is initialized opposite to the expected value.

requirements.definition: The input/output statement set is BACKSPACE, CLOSE, ENDFILE, FLUSH, INQUIRE, OPEN, PRINT, READ, REWIND, WAIT, and WRITE.

requirements.title: Files are record files or stream files by composition
requirements.definition: A file is composed of either file storage units or records; record files are composed of records and stream files are composed of file storage units.

pending.file-storage-unit-composition: Use future unformatted stream access to write a known scalar sequence and inquire POS before and after; assert only monotonic portable position properties named by stream rules, not byte counts.
pending.stream-file-composition: Use future stream access with POS= to read a previously written position; assert only data recovery from an identified position, not storage-unit size.

requirements.title: A processor may expose both record and stream views with processor-dependent correspondence
requirements.definition: A processor may allow the same file to be viewed both as a record file and as a stream file; if so, the relationship between stream file storage units and record-file records is processor dependent.

pending.dual-record-stream-view-permitted: No portable oracle requires that a processor provide both views for a particular external medium; a future profile may document support but must not make it a conformance expectation.
pending.record-stream-correspondence-processor-d: No portable oracle may require a specific mapping between record boundaries and stream positions; future tests must obtain positions through POS= inquiry and avoid comparing to byte counts or newline encodings.
